subject: Energy
title: The Binding Energy Curve
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Binding Energy Curve usable.

hook.text: Every nucleus has a binding energy—the energy needed to tear it apart into individual protons and neutrons.

buildup.text: Iron-56 sits at the peak—it has the highest binding energy per nucleon, making it the most stable nucleus.

discovery.text: Elements lighter than iron release energy by fusing together; elements heavier than iron release energy by splitting.

twist.text: This single curve explains both nuclear fission and fusion—and why stars and reactors both produce energy.

climax.text: Stars fuse hydrogen into iron over millions of years—but can't go further. Iron is the endpoint of stellar fusion.

punchline.text: Iron is the finish line—fusion and fission meet there.

quiz.question: Which element has the highest binding energy per nucleon?
